AR-2026S1-SB1.aiSummary: The law lowers Arkansas income tax rates for individuals, trusts, estates, and corporations. For tax years starting on or after January 1, 2026, it sets new individual tax brackets, and for tax years starting on or after January 1, 2027, it lowers the corporate income tax rate. It became Act 2 on May 6, 2026.

AR-2026F-SB23.aiSummary: The measure became law as Act 133 and sets spending for the Arkansas Department of Human Services' Division of Youth Services for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It provides money for staff, operations, community sanctions, community services, federal child and youth service grants, and residential services, including a total of $14,533,752 for operations and $34,616,356 for residential services. It also allows up to $240,000 for the Juvenile Ombudsman Program and $400,000 for local juvenile detention facilities.

It would take effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-HB1007.aiSummary: This act would set funding for the Arkansas Department of Education’s public school fund for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It would provide money for local school districts, special programs, school employee insurance, teacher pay, student support, technology, and other school aid. The total amount appropriated is $3,662,266,811, and it also sets funding and staff limits for the public school computer network and education renewal zones.
